video.subject_count.evidence: [director·claude] I counted people in every cell from 00:00.000 to 00:21.750 (88 cells). Each cell shows only Riley, one person. Nobody else appears or disappears, and there is no duplicate or twin. She is small and alone in the street at 0–3s, standing alone in mid-frame at 4–14s, and alone in the waist-up framing at 18–21.75s. The cat the spec asks for is not a person, so I handle it under object_continuity.

video.no_text.evidence: [director·claude·审稿兜底，待机检工具] Apart from the yellow timecode added by the review tool in each cell's top-left corner, I found no subtitles, watermark, logo, UI or wall writing at 0–21.75s. The walls are plain red, yellow and white plaster and the doors are plain wooden planks. Caveat: the cells are small, so I can only rule out text that is clearly visible.

video.object_continuity.evidence: [director·claude] (1) The spec's 0s beat requires a cat asleep on the stone step of the northeast corner shop, on the right of frame. In the 00:00.000–00:03.750 cells the right side shows a yellow wall, a dark doorway and a pottery jar. I could not find a cat there or in any later wide cell (for example 06.000 and 10.000), so a required prop is missing. (2) The bread cloth bundle should hang on her left hip, visible whenever she is full-body in frame. In the 0–3s full-body shots the figure is too small to tell. From 16–21s there is a beige tied lump at the front or side of her waist (for example 18.250 and 20.000). I can't tell whether it is the round flat bundle from the prop image on her left hip, or a knotted cloth/belt at the front of her waist. I'm unsure, so I fail it. (3) Several large stone slabs sit diagonally in the foreground (00:00–10:00, lower-left and lower-right of each cell). They break the flat look of a basalt-paved road with raised sidewalks. They don't move, but I can't confirm they are steps or sidewalks that match the scene setup.

video.person_still.evidence: [director·claude·审稿兜底，待机检工具] From 00:06.000 to 00:13.750, about 8 seconds, Riley stands upright in the same spot. In every cell her arms hang at her sides, she makes no gestures, and her full-body pose barely changes. Only the camera's slow push-in changes the framing. The spec has her speaking in this stretch (4.7–13.6s: 'Okay, so… everything's closed… nap time… no idea where I am'), so it is not a scripted quiet beat. At 4fps thumbnail resolution I can't confirm her mouth is moving in sync with the lines, and her body is still well past 1.5s. She reads as a standing figurine, so I fail this and recommend a reshoot that adds gestures and small weight shifts while she talks.

video.point_landed.evidence: [director·claude] With the sound off, here is what I see: a woman walks in from deep in a warm-coloured old street to an empty square where every door is closed. She looks left and right, stands talking to the camera for a long stretch, raises her arm and sniffs her shoulder (14.75–15.75), raises a hand by her face (16.0–16.5), then turns back, spreads her arms in a shrug and smiles (20.5–21.0). The 'stuck in an empty town' idea and the 'smelly sleeve' gag partly come through. Compared against the point and the beats: (1) 'Four identical streets' doesn't land. The camera only ever sees the north street and the facades either side of the junction (0–4s), never the identical east and west streets, so the confusion of looking down four matching streets isn't shown. (2) The walk is wrong. The spec has her already inside the junction at 0s, 1.5m from centre, reaching centre by 1.3s. In the sheet she is still far back in the north street at 0s, very small in frame, and walks until about 2.75–3.0s. Arrival is about 1.5s late and she starts too far away. (3) The push-in is late. The spec has it stop at 15s on a waist-up medium shot. At 15.0 she is still full-body and only reaches waist-up around 18–20s, so the sniff gag plays in a wide shot and its facial reaction (frowning, head jerking back) is too small to read. (4) Her looking-around at 1.3–4s overlaps the walk. (5) The sleeping cat is missing, which weakens the 'nap time, whole town asleep' joke. Shadows are short and the light is midday, which matches.
